EMPIRICAL RESEARCH PLAN  

====================================================  

1. Identification Strategy  
----------------------------------------------------  
Method: “Difference-in-Differences-in-Differences” (DDD) panel design, supplemented with an instrumental-variables (IV) first stage.  

Logic  
• Across industries, we know a priori which ones rely heavily on relationship-specific investments (RS-intensive) from earlier production-function studies (e.g. Nunn 2007 input–output index).  
• Across countries, contract-enforcement quality (CEQ) differs and changes slowly over time.  
• Within a country-year, the difference in exports of RS-intensive vs. RS-non-intensive industries should be larger when CEQ is high—if better contracting truly raises comparative advantage in RS goods.  
• By sweeping out country-year, industry-year, and country-industry fixed effects we obtain the triple difference:  
 β identifies the differential effect of CEQ on RS-intensive industries, relative to the same country, same year, and same industry elsewhere.  
• To guard against reverse causality (trade performance → legal reforms) we 2SLS the continuous CEQ measure with an exogenous legal-origin instrument interacted with RS-dependence (La Porta et al. legal-origin dummies are time-invariant and pre-date modern trade patterns).  

Main estimating equation (second stage):  

log Trade_{c,i,t} = β (RS_i × CEQ_{c,t}) + γ_i,t + δ_c,t + θ_{c,i} + X_{c,i,t}′ϕ + ε_{c,i,t}  

where γ_i,t = industry-year FE, δ_c,t = country-year FE, θ_{c,i} = country-industry FE.  

2. Treatment and Control  
----------------------------------------------------  
Treatment variable RS_i × CEQ_{c,t}  
• RS_i – continuous index of relationship specificity (top quartile sometimes used for binary robustness).  
• CEQ_{c,t} – World Bank “Rule of Law” or “Contract Enforcement” (Doing Business) score, 0–100, demeaned.  

Control group  
• (Within-country-year) all industries with low RS_i.  
• (Within-industry-year) the same industry in countries with low CEQ.  

Timing  
• Annual panel 1995–2020. No single event date; the treatment intensity varies continuously each year.  

IV first stage  
• Z_{c} = Legal-Origin dummies (English, French, German, Socialist, Scandinavian) × RS_i.  

3. Key Identifying Assumptions  
----------------------------------------------------  
A1. Conditional Parallel Trends – In the absence of differences in CEQ, exports of RS- and non-RS goods would grow in parallel within each country-year. Time-varying country shocks are absorbed by country-year FE; industry shocks by industry-year FE. Plausible.  

A2. Exogeneity of Instrument – Legal origin affects current trade only through its effect on CEQ, not through other channels once country-industry FE are included. Historically grounded; still debatable but standard.  

A3. Stable RS-dependence – RS_i is technology-driven and invariant over time. Supported by empirical work (input specificity changes slowly).  

4. Main Threats & Remedies  
----------------------------------------------------  
T1. Reverse causality / omitted economic development.  
  Remedy: IV with legal origin; add GDP pc, human-capital, and capital-intensity controls interacted with RS_i.  

T2. Measurement error in CEQ (survey based).  
  Remedy: Use multiple CEQ series (Doing Business, WGI, PRS); instrument; cluster at country level.  

T3. Global supply-chain shocks correlated with RS industries (e.g., ICT revolution).  
  Remedy: industry-year FE already capture any worldwide industry shock; additionally interact year dummies with WTO membership.  

5. R Code Outline  
----------------------------------------------------  
```r
# Packages
library(data.table)
library(fixest)      # fast TWFE & IV
library(readr)

# 1. Load data --------------------------------------------------------------
com  <- fread("comtrade_panel.csv")      # country, partner, industry, year, value
wdi  <- fread("wdi_ceq.csv")             # country, year, ceq, gdp_pc, etc.
rs   <- fread("industry_RSindex.csv")    # industry, RS_index

# 2. Merge & construct ------------------------------------------------------
panel <- merge(com, wdi, by = c("country","year"))
panel <- merge(panel, rs,  by = "industry")

# Basic cleaning
panel <- panel[!is.na(value) & value > 0]
panel[, ltrade := log(value)]

# Treatment intensity & instrument
panel[, treat        := RS_index * ceq]       # continuous DD
panel[, legal_fr     := as.integer(legal_origin == "French")]
panel[, z_inst       := RS_index * legal_fr]  # first IV (add others similarly)

# 3. Main specification -----------------------------------------------------
est_main <- feols(ltrade ~ 1 | country^industry + country^year + industry^year |
                  treat |               # endogenous regressor
                  z_inst,                # IV(s)
                  data = panel,
                  cluster = "country")

summary(est_main)

# 4. Robustness: binary treatment & placebo ---------------------------------
panel[, high_RS := as.integer(RS_index > quantile(RS_index, .75))]
panel[, high_CEQ := as.integer(ceq > median(ceq)), by = year]
panel[, treat_bin := high_RS * high_CEQ]

est_rb <- feols(ltrade ~ treat_bin | country^industry + country^year + industry^year,
                data = panel, cluster = "country")
summary(est_rb)

# 5. Event-study type robustness: lead-lag ----------------------------------
panel[, ceq_lead2 := shift(ceq,  2), by = country]
panel[, ceq_lag2  := shift(ceq, -2), by = country]
panel[, treat_lead2 := RS_index * ceq_lead2]

est_lead <- feols(ltrade ~ treat_lead2 | country^industry + country^year + industry^year,
                  data=panel, cluster="country")
summary(est_lead)
```

6. Expected Results  
----------------------------------------------------  
Theory (Grossman-Helpman, Antràs) predicts β > 0: better enforcement raises exports in RS-intensive industries. Magnitude: a 1 sd increase in CEQ (≈0.15 on 0–1 scale) for an industry at the 75th percentile of RS dependence (≈0.6) should raise exports by roughly 5-10 percent (elasticity 0.07).  

7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (DDD + IV)  
----------------------------------------------------  
C1: Parallel trends within country-year after FE 1  
C2: No simultaneous shocks correlated with RS_i × CEQ 0.5  
C3: Instrument relevance (legal origin → CEQ) 1  
C4: Instrument exclusion (legal origin ⟂ trade except through CEQ) 0.5  
C5: No spillovers / SUTVA across country-industry pairs 1  

Total = 4/5 → Reasonably credible though exclusion restriction warrants scrutiny.
